confidence_notes: FX is the weakest input: I could not retrieve any current RBA daily observation. The value used is the latest RBA figure my search returned (20 March 2026), so it is about seven months old and may not be the latest published rate. I did not use the OFX quotes or a Banque de France-derived cross rate because neither is an RBA observation. Food anchors rest on undated or mixed-quality aggregated sources: an Expatistan pub-beer estimate (updated 2025-2026, based on few data points), a crowd-sourced cappuccino average from a 2026 price-comparison page (citing Numbeo), a World Travel Guide meal-for-two band of unknown date, and an undated Expatistan Italian dinner estimate. No Delhi-specific current wine or cocktail prices were found, so cocktail and wine anchors are set from the local beer relationship (cocktail about twice the beer price, wine glass near the cocktail level) and are the least certain food values. The inexpensive-meal anchor is a judgement from the cheap-band reference and local dining patterns, because the Numbeo India figure I found dates from about 2015. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge; I did not check live booking pages or current listings and did not search for accommodation prices.
comparable_city_reasoning: No comparable city was used. Food and drink anchors use Delhi-specific aggregated reference points where available, with the beer relationship for cocktail and wine. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates for a large Indian metropolis with a budget-hotel and hostel market and a separate upscale tier, based on general knowledge only.
